contributor_notes: Documentary chronicling ACT UP and TAG activism during the early AIDS crisis (1980s-90s). The source text does not name individual activists, so no specific queer characters are tagged here — a maintainer with access to the footage/subjects could add named real-life activists with appropriate sourcing. The film centers the gay community and AIDS activism, hence 'own-voices' and 'period-piece' tags, though a maintainer should verify creator identities before confirming own-voices. Trigger warnings drawn from stated content: AIDS-related deaths/illness (hiv-aids, character-death) and depiction of discriminatory policies against HIV-positive individuals (homophobia). Note: AIDS historian Sarah Schulman criticized the film for focusing predominantly on wealthy white activists rather than the full diversity of ACT UP — relevant to representation/humility discussions. No subtitle or audio language info was provided in the source.
